supported_diagnosis: The correction fields and unchanged system prompt reached each recorded client request; they were not omitted by local message construction.

Every attempt remained a new two-turn system/user exchange. The previous invalid proposal and the corrective error were embedded as JSON context data rather than an assistant reply followed by an explicit corrective user turn.
The validator fails at the first forbid/final conflict, so the subsequent current-visible-expect violation was not included in the concrete correction error.
JSON-object response formatting enforces syntax, not semantic postcondition consistency; independent local rejection remains necessary.
inferences_not_proven: The two-turn nested correction may have encouraged repetition or made correction less salient; a controlled saved-frame chat-repair probe is needed to test this.

The model may be interpreting forbid_text as do-not-click/do-not-repeat rather than text that must be absent after the operation. The forbidden values match completed results, but its internal interpretation cannot be established from output alone.
generic_repair_recommendation: Keep the source unchanged until Root validates explicit chat correction using the same archived frame, whole instruction and caller final checks.

If the probe succeeds, represent the invalid proposal as an assistant turn and add a last user correction turn listing all detected field-level constraint violations; continue to count every transport attempt and retain every reply.

Clarify generic postcondition semantics: expect_text must be present after the goal, forbid_text must be absent after the goal; forbid_text does not mean an operation should not be repeated or a completed context is irrelevant.
